workflows.name: Load help center pages into a Pinecone knowledge base with OpenAI embeddings
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow manually fetches help pages (or demo docs), chunks them, generates OpenAI embeddings, and upserts the vectors into a Pinecone index so they can be used for retrieval-based support or chat.

How it works
Starts when you run the workflow manually.
Reads configuration to decide whether to load URLs from DOC_URLS or use the built-in demo knowledge base.
Fetches each public document URL with retries, converts the HTML to plain text, and records any pages that fail or contain too little text.
Splits each document into overlapping text chunks with stable chunk IDs so re-running updates existing vectors instead of duplicating them.
If OpenAI/Pinecone loading is not enabled (for example, preview mode or missing configuration), outputs the chunks that would be embedded and upserted without writing anything.
Otherwise, batches chunks, calls the OpenAI Embeddings API to create vectors, and skips any batches that fail to embed after retries.
Upserts each successfully embedded batch into Pinecone with title, source, and chunk text stored as metadata, and reports either the upsert counts or the Pinecone error.

Setup
Add an OpenAI API credential in n8n and set USE_OPENAI to true in the config node.
Create a Pinecone index whose vector dimension matches EMBED_DIMENSIONS, then add a Pinecone HTTP Header Auth credential (Api-Key) and set PINECONE_INDEX_HOST and PINECONE_NAMESPACE in the config node.
Add your public documentation URLs to DOC_URLS and adjust CHUNK_WORDS/CHUNK_OVERLAP if you want different chunking behavior.
Switch out of preview mode (set TEST_EMAIL for test mode or set TEST_RUN to false) so upserts are enabled.

workflows.name: Answer Gmail support emails with OpenAI and a Pinecone knowledge base
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow monitors a Gmail inbox for new unread messages, classifies them with OpenAI (or keyword rules), searches a Pinecone knowledge base for relevant help content, and either replies in the original Gmail thread or escalates the case to a support team address.

How it works
Triggers every minute when an unread email arrives in a Gmail inbox (excluding messages sent from your own account).
Normalizes the email into a clean format (sender, subject, new message text, thread/message IDs) and drops auto-replies, empty emails, or messages without a usable sender.
Classifies the message as support or not-support using OpenAI Chat Completions (with a keyword fallback) and routes non-support emails out without replying.
Escalates sensitive or uncertain cases (for example complaints, refunds, legal, cancellations, or low-confidence classifications) by preparing an internal alert email for the support team.
For answerable support requests, embeds the question with OpenAI and queries Pinecone for the top matching knowledge chunks (or uses a built-in demo knowledge base when Pinecone is not configured).
If the best knowledge match is above the configured score threshold, drafts a reply using OpenAI constrained to the retrieved excerpts (or a template reply when OpenAI is disabled), otherwise escalates to a person.
Depending on preview/test/live mode, either shows the drafted reply without sending, emails a test copy to a specified address, or replies to the customer in the original Gmail thread.

Setup
Connect Gmail credentials for the Gmail Trigger and Gmail send/reply actions, and ensure the trigger query matches the inbox you want to monitor.
Add an OpenAI API credential for the HTTP Request steps (chat completions and embeddings) and set your chosen chat and embedding models in the config node if you change defaults.
Create a Pinecone index with the configured embedding dimensions (default 1536) and add a Pinecone Header Auth credential (Api-Key), then set the Pinecone index host and namespace in the config node.
Update the config node with your support team escalation address, your own “do not reply” sender addresses, and tune the confidence and match-score thresholds to control when the workflow is allowed to auto-reply.
Start in preview or test mode by setting TEST_RUN/TEST_EMAIL in the config node, then switch to live mode only after verifying replies and escalations behave as expected.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow receives incoming Twilio WhatsApp messages, looks up gold chain availability and last-approved prices from Google Sheets (or built-in demo stock), optionally uses an OpenAI-compatible model to parse what the customer wants, and replies with matching in-stock items or escalates complex requests to the owner.

How it works
Receives an inbound WhatsApp message via a Twilio webhook (or uses built-in demo messages when run manually).
Loads the current catalogue from a Google Sheets Stock tab, or falls back to the workflow’s demo stock data if no sheet is configured.
Parses the customer’s text to extract style, karat, length, and quantity using keyword rules, optionally refining those fields with an OpenAI-compatible chat completion request.
Builds a response based on the sheet data: confirms opt-out requests, escalates bulk/orders/custom/complaints to the owner, or returns up to three closest in-stock matches with quantities and list prices.
Routes messages based on mode (preview/test/live) and sends replies and owner alerts through Twilio WhatsApp, or outputs a preview when sending is disabled.
If the customer opted out and live writing is enabled, updates the Google Sheets Customers tab to mark the WhatsApp number as opted out.

Setup
Create a Twilio WhatsApp sender and configure Twilio’s “A message comes in” webhook to POST to this workflow’s webhook URL.
Add Twilio credentials in n8n and set your WhatsApp sender number in TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM and your escalation number in OWNER_WHATSAPP in the config.
Create a Google Sheet with Stock and Customers tabs (and the expected columns), add Google Sheets credentials in n8n, and set SHEET_ID in the config.
(Optional) Add an OpenAI API key (or compatible endpoint) and set AI_API_KEY, AI_BASE_URL, and AI_MODEL in the config to improve message parsing.
Choose your run mode by setting TEST_RUN and (optionally) TEST_WHATSAPP in the config before switching to live sending and writing.

user.name: muhd dahlan
user.bio: Muhd Dahlan is an AI solution architect and engineering leader with experience across artificial intelligence, blockchain, and financial technology. workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow reprices a gold chain stock list every weekday using a daily gold rate from goldapi.io (or a demo rate), builds a WhatsApp-ready catalogue and “what changed” announcement, and uses Twilio WhatsApp to request owner approval before broadcasting to customers and optionally updating a Google Sheets stock sheet.

How it works
Runs every weekday at 08:00 (or manually) and loads business, pricing, sheet, and WhatsApp settings from a single configuration step.
Reads stock rows from Google Sheets (or uses built-in demo stock) and holds back any items that can’t be priced due to missing weight, unknown style, or unsupported karat.
Fetches today’s 24k gold price per gram from goldapi.io (or uses a labeled demo rate) and prices each chain, stopping if the rate looks implausible compared to the previous published rate.
Builds a customer-facing catalogue, an internal stock list/CSV, and a short announcement message that includes only changes such as new items, back in stock, last few, and sold out.
Reads the customer list from Google Sheets (or uses demo customers), filters out opted-out/invalid/duplicate numbers, enforces a broadcast cap, and prepares one WhatsApp message per recipient.
Sends the draft announcement to the owner on WhatsApp via Twilio with an approval link, then broadcasts the approved message to customers (or outputs a preview when sending is disabled).
If live mode is enabled, writes today’s price, rate, quantity, and timestamp back to the Google Sheets Stock tab so the next run can detect changes.

Setup
Add Twilio credentials in n8n and set your Twilio WhatsApp sender number plus the owner’s WhatsApp number in the config so the approval request and broadcasts can be delivered.
Create a Google Sheet with “Stock” and “Customers” tabs (matching the expected columns) and set the Sheet ID and tab names in the config, then connect Google Sheets OAuth on the Google Sheets nodes.
Create a goldapi.io API key and enter it in the config along with your target currency to fetch the daily 24k gold rate.
Review and tailor pricing inputs in the config (PURITY table, STYLES making charges, margin, rounding, LOW_STOCK_AT, BROADCAST_CAP, and APPROVAL_WAIT_HOURS).
Start in preview/test by keeping TEST_RUN enabled (optionally set TEST_WHATSAPP to redirect sends), then switch to live by setting TEST_RUN to false once you are ready to send and write updates.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs twice on weekdays (or manually) to read an order board in Google Sheets, pull tracking details from the sheet or ShipStation, and send shipping notification emails through Gmail, then updates the sheet so each shipped order is only emailed once.

How it works
Runs on a weekday schedule at 08:30 and 16:30 (or via a manual trigger) and loads shared configuration values.
Reads the Orders tab from Google Sheets, or uses built-in demo rows when the sheet is not yet connected.
Identifies orders marked as Shipped that have a confirmation timestamp and have not yet been sent a shipping email, and separately flags any Shipped orders with no confirmation.
For each eligible shipped order, uses the tracking number from the Google Sheet if present, otherwise fetches carrier, tracking, and ship date from the ShipStation API when configured.
Stops the run for any order where no tracking number can be found, to avoid sending a shipping email without tracking.
Composes a personalized shipping email with tracking details and installation information, then either sends it via Gmail (test or live) or holds it in preview mode.
After a successful send, writes the carrier, tracking, ship date, and “Ship email sent” timestamp back to Google Sheets to prevent duplicate emails.

Setup
Provide a Google Sheets credential and fill in the spreadsheet ID and tab name in the config so the workflow can read and update your Orders board.
Provide a Gmail credential and set the sender details (from name and optional reply-to) in the config.
Ensure your Google Sheet contains the expected columns (including Stage, Confirmation sent, Carrier, Tracking no., Shipped date, and Ship email sent) and that the office sets Stage to Shipped to queue an email.
(Optional) Add ShipStation API credentials and enable ShipStation in the config to look up tracking automatically when it is not pasted into the sheet.
Review the TEST_RUN / TEST_EMAIL settings in the config to run in preview, test, or live mode before activating the schedule.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow receives Shopify, Etsy, or Square order webhooks, normalizes them into a single order format, logs new orders to a Google Sheets “Orders” tab, and sends a confirmation email via Gmail (with preview/test modes), then updates the sheet to mark the order as confirmed.

How it works
Receives an order payload via a Webhook endpoint and loads shared settings (sheet IDs, product rules, and email mode) from the configuration.
Detects whether the payload is from Shopify, Etsy, or Square, extracts a common set of order fields, and rejects orders missing required data (and holds Square orders until the deposit is paid).
Reads existing rows from Google Sheets (or a built-in demo board if the sheet is not enabled) and checks whether the order key already exists to prevent duplicate logging.
Validates each line item against the configured product rules and calculates a working-day shipping window from the longest lead time plus buffers, holding orders that contain unknown SKUs when enabled.
Builds a single-row “board” record and composes a customer confirmation email that includes the planned shipping window when available.
Appends the order row to Google Sheets, optionally sends the confirmation email via Gmail (live or redirected to a test address), and then updates the sheet to set the order stage to Confirmed with a confirmation timestamp.
Responds to the original webhook request with a JSON acknowledgement so the storefront stops retrying.

Setup
Create a Google Sheet with an “Orders” tab that matches the column headings expected in the workflow configuration (for example: Order key, Source, Order no., Placed, Email, Items (json), Ship window start/end, Stage, Confirmation sent).
In the config node, set your Google Sheets document ID and tab name and switch BOARD_READY to true (otherwise the workflow runs in demo/preview mode).
Add Google Sheets credentials for the Google Sheets nodes and Gmail credentials for the Gmail send node.
Configure your Shopify, Etsy, and/or Square webhook to POST to this workflow’s production Webhook URL path (order-in).
Review and maintain PRODUCT_RULES (SKUs, lead times, manuals/notes) and set TEST_RUN/TEST_EMAIL to control preview, test, or live sending behavior.

workflows.name: Export Instagram follower and following change history to CSV with Instoryview

user.name: Instoryview
user.bio: Instoryview helps creators and social media teams review stored follower and following snapshots and detected changes for supported public Instagram accounts. Our workflow templates turn saved tracking data into useful reports through the Instoryview API.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
Export stored follower or following change history for a tracked Instagram account with Instoryview. This manual workflow generates a CSV, including a header-only file for empty results, and a JSON summary with data coverage and warnings.

How it works
Starts when you manually execute the workflow.
Sets the tracked Instagram username, whether to export followers or following changes, and an inclusive date range with timezone.
Validates the settings and builds the Instoryview changes API request URL.
Calls the Instoryview Open API to fetch all change-history pages using cursor pagination (up to 100 pages with a 1.5-second interval).
Checks page completeness and account and date-range consistency, then prepares normalized event rows and a JSON summary. Duplicate events, changing summaries, or incomplete pagination stop the export.
Creates a CSV file from the change rows, or generates an empty CSV containing only headers when no changes are returned.

Setup
Track the target Instagram account in Instoryview and wait for tracking history to accumulate.
Create an API key with the data:read scope in Instoryview Developer settings. In Read all change pages, create or select an n8n Header Auth credential: header name Authorization, header value Bearer YOUR_API_KEY.
Update the Export settings values (username, followers/following, from/to dates, and timezone) to match what you want to export.

Requirements
An Instoryview account with access to the selected tracked account and its retained change history, a data:read API key, and n8n with the built-in HTTP Request, Code, and Convert to File nodes.

Customization
Choose followers or following, an inclusive date range of up to 366 days, and an IANA timezone. Import CSV ID columns as Text to preserve long Instagram IDs.

Additional info
These API reads use zero new collection credits and never initiate a paid lookup or create tracking. Detected timestamps record when Instoryview observed a change, not the exact Instagram action time. Fetching all pages does not make partial or unknown tracking history complete. The workflow stops on HTTP errors or unfinished pagination at its 100-page ceiling; reduce the date range and rerun. Changes cursors expire after 15 minutes. See the changes API guide for coverage and error details.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow collects company and role inputs via an n8n Form, discovers the company domain, scrapes the website, Google News RSS, and Hacker News, then uses Google Gemini to synthesize a structured interview dossier and renders it as a printable, downloadable HTML “PDF-style” report with charts and diagrams.

How it works
Receives company name, optional website URL, target role, and optional job description from an n8n Form submission.
Uses Clearbit Autocomplete to auto-discover the company domain (or falls back to the provided URL) and generates logo and website screenshot URLs via Clearbit Logo and WordPress MShots.
Scrapes the company website text through Jina Reader while also fetching recent headlines from Google News RSS and related threads from the Hacker News Algolia API.
Aggregates the scraped content into a single research context that includes source URLs for news items and discussion threads.
Sends the context to Google Gemini to generate a JSON interview dossier with ratings, key metrics, a Mermaid ecosystem diagram, and a verified evidence log.
Builds a printable HTML dossier that embeds a QuickChart radar chart, a Mermaid.ink-rendered diagram, the website snapshot, and clickable citations, then displays it in the browser and also creates an HTML file for download.

Setup
Add Google Gemini (PaLM) API credentials for the Google Gemini Chat Model node.
Ensure the workflow’s n8n Form trigger is accessible to users who will submit requests (and share the form URL as needed).
If you want to avoid domain-guess fallbacks, provide a company website URL in the form or confirm Clearbit Autocomplete can resolve your target companies.
Verify outbound network access to Clearbit Autocomplete/Logo, Jina Reader (r.jina.ai), WordPress MShots, Google News RSS, Hacker News Algolia, QuickChart, and Mermaid.ink in your environment.

Quick overview
This workflow finds underperforming pages in Google Search Console, generates improved SEO titles and meta descriptions with OpenAI based on real query data, logs suggestions in Google Sheets for review, and can optionally write approved updates back to WordPress (Yoast or Rank Math).

How it works
Runs weekly (or manually) to generate new suggestions, and runs hourly to process approved rows from Google Sheets.
Reads the existing “SEO Log” tab in Google Sheets to enforce a cooldown window and avoid re-suggesting recently updated URLs.
Queries the Google Search Console Search Analytics API for page-level performance, scores pages by missed clicks versus a position-based CTR benchmark, and selects the worst offenders.
Looks up matching WordPress posts/pages by slug and maps each candidate URL to a WordPress ID and content type for optional write-back.
For each candidate page, pulls its top queries from Google Search Console and fetches the live HTML to extract the current title, meta description, and H1.
Uses OpenAI Chat to produce a new SEO title, an alternative title, and a meta description (with a length check), then appends the suggestion to Google Sheets with status set to “pending”.
On hourly runs, reads “approved” rows from Google Sheets and either updates the Yoast/Rank Math meta fields via the WordPress REST API and marks them “applied”, or marks them “manual” if write-back is disabled or the page can’t be matched.

Setup
Add Google OAuth2 credentials with the Search Console scope (https://www.googleapis.com/auth/webmasters.readonly) for the Google Search Console HTTP requests.
Add a Google Sheets OAuth connection, create a spreadsheet tab named “SEO Log” with the expected columns, and set the sheet ID and tab name in the config.
Add OpenAI credentials (or swap the chat model node) and confirm the model selection used for generating titles and descriptions.
If you want automatic updates, add WordPress API credentials (Application Password), set seo_plugin to “yoast” or “rank_math”, and ensure the relevant post meta keys are exposed in the WordPress REST API.
Update the config values for gsc_property, wp_base_url, language, and any filtering limits (lookback_days, min_impressions, max_position, ctr_ratio, max_per_run, cooldown_days) before enabling the schedule triggers.

workflows.name: Reply to WhatsApp sales leads with OpenAI, Supabase, and Slack alerts

user.name: Bhaskar Gorati
user.bio: AI Automation Engineer specializing in n8n, AI agents, and intelligent workflow automation. I build practical automation systems that connect AI models, APIs, business applications, and data to solve real-world business problems. I also share n8n workflows, AI automation projects, and practical tutorials to help others build with n8n.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow receives WhatsApp Cloud API messages, uses OpenAI to generate grounded sales replies, logs and scores each lead in Supabase, and notifies your team in Slack when a lead is hot or needs a human.

How it works
Receives WhatsApp Cloud API webhook calls for inbound messages and handles Meta’s one-time webhook verification challenge.
Normalizes the incoming WhatsApp payload into a clean customer message record and ignores non-message status callbacks.
Checks Supabase to deduplicate by WhatsApp message ID, then looks up (or creates) the customer record by phone number and pulls recent conversation history.
Loads the product catalog from Supabase and sends the customer message, recent history, and business info to an OpenAI-backed agent to classify intent and draft a short reply.
Applies rule-based lead scoring to label the conversation Cold/Warm/Hot and prepares the final response payload.
Sends the AI reply back to the customer on WhatsApp, saves the conversation in Supabase, updates the customer CRM fields, and posts a Slack alert when the lead is Hot or the agent flags that a human is needed.

Setup
Configure Meta WhatsApp Cloud API to call the workflow’s webhook URL and set the same verify token in Meta and in the webhook verification response logic.
Add credentials for Supabase, OpenAI, and Slack, and ensure the Slack OAuth connection can post to your chosen channel.
Create Supabase tables for customers, conversations, and products (including fields used for phone, message_id, timestamps, product_name, and any stored prices), then populate products with your catalog.
Update the client-specific values in the business configuration (business name, WhatsApp phone number ID, Slack channel ID, and delivery/payment/returns/hours/contact details).

Requirements
WhatsApp Business API access: a Meta Business account with the WhatsApp Cloud API enabled, a phone number ID, an access token, and the webhook set to your n8n URL with the messages field subscribed and a verify token.
Supabase project: the three tables (customers, conversations, products) created with whatsapp_sales_agent_setup.sql, plus a Supabase credential in n8n.
Products and business facts: the client’s product list (name, price, description, features, stock) in the products table. Their delivery, payment, return and hours details go in Client Config.
OpenAI API key: an OpenAI credential in n8n. The agent uses gpt-4o-mini.
Slack alerts: a Slack app invited to the sales channel, plus that channel’s ID, so Hot leads and human requests reach the client’s team.

Customization
Business details: edit Client Config for the business name, phone number ID, Slack channel, delivery areas and time, payment methods, return policy and hours.
Reply style: edit the system prompt in AI Sales Agent to change the tone, language (English, Hindi, Telugu, Hinglish), reply length, emojis or the sign-off.
Lead scoring: edit the points and the Hot/Warm/Cold cut-offs (70 and 40 by default) in AI Lead Scoring. Add the client’s own buying keywords.
Alert rules: change the condition in Hot Lead or Human Needed?, for example alert only on Hot, or on every purchase intent. Swap Slack for email or WhatsApp if the client prefers.
Catalog size: the workflow loads only the first 30 products. For a bigger catalog, add a filter on the customer’s product interest or the search words in their message.

workflows.name: Send Hyperliquid wallet fill alerts to Telegram
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Monitor one public Hyperliquid wallet every five minutes and receive Telegram summaries of new fills. Alerts show recent trades and perpetual position changes, with a link to inspect the same address in the Market Depth Lab wallet tracker.

How it works
Runs every five minutes (or manually in preview mode).
Loads the target Hyperliquid wallet address, a label, and the Telegram chat ID, then validates inputs and restores the last saved checkpoint when available.
Queries the Hyperliquid Info API (userFillsByTime) for fills within a bounded time window that includes a small overlap to catch late-indexed records.
Validates and deduplicates returned fills, filters out anything already seen or older than the baseline, and formats up to six of the latest fills into a Telegram HTML message.
Sends one Telegram alert per batch only during scheduled monitoring, after the first silent baseline run. Manual preview never sends messages. Each alert displays at most six fills; any additional fills are counted and marked as processed.
Advances the checkpoint only after confirmed Telegram delivery or a successful check with no alert needed. Workflow static data persists after successful active/published production executions; manual previews do not change stored state.

Setup
Enter the public Hyperliquid wallet address (0x…), a label, and your Telegram chat ID in the Wallet settings.
Create/select Telegram bot credentials in n8n and ensure the bot can post to the target chat (and use the correct chat ID).
Run Preview manually and inspect the final node output. This reads recent fills without sending a message or saving state. When ready, activate scheduled monitoring: the first successful scheduled run is silent. Check execution history and avoid concurrent runs.

Requirements
An n8n instance, a public Hyperliquid master-account or subaccount address, and a Telegram bot credential with permission to message the destination chat. No wallet connection, private key, or Hyperliquid trading API key is needed.

Customization
Change the wallet address and label in Wallet settings. Use one lower-volume wallet per workflow and keep the five-minute interval with sequential executions. Connect an n8n error workflow if you need failure notifications.

Additional info
Created by Market Depth Lab. Each alert opens the monitored address in the Market Depth Lab Hyperliquid Wallet Tracker.

Scope: returned fills only, not deposits, withdrawals, funding, or a complete portfolio. Spot pair codes and returned HIP-3 prefixes are preserved.

Static-data persistence is experimental. Interrupted deliveries can cause duplicate alerts; fills arriving after the overlap window may be missed. This version does not paginate: responses of 500 or more fills, malformed responses, or checkpoint gaps over 24 hours stop with an error. It is designed for lower-volume wallets, not high-frequency or concurrent monitoring.

workflows.name: Send crypto price spike alerts with CoinGecko, OpenAI, and Telegram

user.name: Ali Abdullah
user.bio: AI Engineer (FDE) & AI Automation Expert. I build autonomous agents, RAG pipelines, and workflow automations that run in production, not demos. Verified n8n Creator. I take AI from pilot to deployed across live business operations. No slideware, only shipped systems.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
Crypto holders, traders, and anyone watching the market who wants instant alerts when something moves hard, without staring at charts all day.

How it works
Every 6 hours the workflow pulls the top 30 coins by market cap from the free CoinGecko API (no API key needed) and flags any coin whose 24h price moved beyond your threshold, 5 percent by default. It ranks the movers by size of move, then OpenAI writes a sharp plain-language take on what might be driving the moves. Everything is formatted into a clean Markdown alert, AI take first, then the movers with prices and percentages, and sent to your Telegram chat. If nothing moved beyond your threshold, the workflow ends quietly with no alert.

Setup
1. Get an OpenAI API key from platform.openai.com and add it as credentials on the AI Market Take node. 2. Create a Telegram bot with @BotFather and copy the API token. 3. Get your chat ID (message @userinfobot on Telegram). 4. In n8n, add your Telegram credentials on the Send Telegram Alert node. 5. Open the Configuration node and paste your chat ID. 6. Press Execute on the manual trigger to test, then activate the workflow.

Requirements
An OpenAI API key (used for the AI market take step). A Telegram bot token and your Telegram chat ID. Nothing else: market data comes from a free public API, so no other keys are needed.

Customization
Raise or lower the spike threshold, track more or fewer coins, or change the check frequency in the Configuration node. Swap the Telegram node for Slack, Discord, or email to change how alerts are delivered.

workflows.name: Upsert Lection scrape results into Google Sheets with webhook deduplication
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow receives Lection scheduled-scrape webhook events and writes the returned dataset records into Google Sheets, deduplicating by a chosen unique column using an upsert operation.

How it works
Receives a POST webhook from Lection for a scheduled scrape delivery.
Verifies the request by comparing the x-lection-secret header against a configured shared secret and returns 401 if it does not match.
Checks that the event is scheduled_scrape.completed and that the dataset contains at least one row, otherwise returns a JSON response indicating nothing was written.
Splits the incoming body.dataset.records array into individual items.
Upserts each record into Google Sheets using “append or update” based on the configured matching (unique) column.
Aggregates the write results and responds to Lection with a JSON payload including how many rows were written.

Setup
Create a Google Sheet with a header row whose column names exactly match the field names in Lection’s dataset.records.
Add a Google Sheets OAuth2 credential in n8n and set the target Spreadsheet ID and sheet name in the Google Sheets node.
Set the matching (unique) column used for deduplication in the Google Sheets node’s matching columns setting.
Configure the expected webhook secret in the workflow (or remove the secret check) and set the same secret in Lection’s webhook delivery settings.
Copy the workflow’s production webhook URL and configure it as the Webhook delivery channel for your Lection scheduled scrape, ensuring the webhook path matches your setup.

Requirements
A Lection account on a paid plan (webhook delivery is paid-only), with a scheduled scrape that has a stable unique column

Additional info
Activate the workflow and use its production webhook URL, not the test URL. Test sends from Lection are acknowledged but never written, so use Run now in Lection to check the mapping. Sheet column names are case-sensitive. If you pick the n8n destination in Lection, which has no secret field, delete the Secret matches? node.

user.name: Swapnil Mandloi
user.bio: AI Automation Engineer specializing in low-code pipelines and custom n8n orchestrations. I help businesses eliminate manual bottlenecks by building scalable, node-based workflows and smart CRM integrations. Reach out to streamline your operations or build custom AI pipelines!

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow receives motorsports tech-inspection submissions via webhook, scores each safety item against expiry rules, uses OpenAI to classify the overall outcome (Pass/Conditional/Fail/Disqualify), then posts results to a race-control timing API, archives to Google Sheets, and notifies Slack.

How it works
Receives a POST request from a trackside tech-inspection app containing car details, inspector notes, and an array of safety-equipment items.
Splits the equipment array into individual items and calculates days-to-expiry and pass/fail per item based on class-specific renewal cycles.
Adds a human-readable class/rating label to each item and aggregates the per-item results back into a consolidated per-car compliance summary.
Sends the compliance summary and inspector notes to an OpenAI-powered text classifier to route the car into Pass, Conditional-Pass-Rework, Fail, or Disqualify.
Writes the chosen inspection category into an inspectionCategory field and routes to the matching outcome path.
For Pass outcomes, checks the provided grid-eligibility cutoff timestamp and posts a PASS result with a gridEligible flag to the race-control timing API.
For Conditional-Pass-Rework, Fail, and Disqualify outcomes, posts the corresponding result to the race-control timing API, escalates Disqualify to a chief-steward Slack channel, then appends the final result to Google Sheets and notifies the tech-inspection crew on Slack.

Setup
Create an OpenAI credential and select it on the OpenAI Chat Model used by the inspection text classifier.
Create an HTTP Header Auth credential for your race-control timing system and replace the example API base URL in all HTTP Request steps.
Connect Google Sheets OAuth credentials, set the spreadsheet ID, and ensure the Tech_Inspection_Archive sheet exists for appending inspection logs.
Connect Slack credentials, set the chief-steward and tech-crew channel IDs, and confirm the workflow can post messages to both channels.
Copy the webhook URL for the tech-inspection-submission path into your trackside app and ensure the payload includes equipmentItems, inspectorNotes, carNumber, and gridEligibilityCutoff (plus any fields your timing payload expects).
Review and adjust the equipment expiry-cycle map in the code step (e.g., helmet/harness cycles) to match your sanctioning body’s rules.

workflows.name: Classify FRA track defects, route tag-out approvals, and archive records with OpenAI, Slack, and Google Drive

user.name: Swapnil Mandloi
user.bio: AI Automation Engineer specializing in low-code pipelines and custom n8n orchestrations. I help businesses eliminate manual bottlenecks by building scalable, node-based workflows and smart CRM integrations. Reach out to streamline your operations or build custom AI pipelines!

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow automates daily railway track safety management by integrating defect classification, risk calculations, and communication. It uses OpenAI to categorize inspector notes by FRA severity, determines speed restrictions, and orchestrates critical Slack approvals for immediate tag-outs, before archiving records to Google Drive and posting final inspection summaries.

How it works
Runs every day at 05:00 on a schedule.
Fetches all segments due for inspection for the current date from the track-inspection system API and processes each segment as a separate item.
Uses OpenAI to classify each segment’s inspector defect notes into one of four categories: No Defect, Class 1-2 Minor, Class 3-4 Serious, or Class 5 Immediate Halt.
Computes the normal maximum speed, any required speed restriction, a remedial timeframe, and a recommended action based on the segment’s track class and defect category.
For Class 5 Immediate Halt segments, sends a Slack approval request that lets a supervisor approve, approve with edits, or reject the tag-out; for all other categories, marks the record as not requiring approval.
Uploads a JSON record for each segment and outcome to Google Drive and posts the final category, action, and speed restriction to a Slack channel.

Setup
Add credentials for the track-inspection system API (HTTP Header Auth), OpenAI, Slack, and Google Drive.
Replace the track-inspection API URL in the HTTP request node and ensure the response includes segment_id, track_class, and inspector_defect_notes as one item per segment.
Set your Slack channel ID in both Slack message nodes and confirm Slack “send and wait for approval” is enabled for your workspace.
Set the target Google Drive drive ID and folder ID for the archive upload.
Review and adjust the track-class speed table and remedial-day defaults in the speed restriction calculation code to match your railroad’s policy.
